answer: Random-walk trust scoring resists sybils: short random walks launched from a trusted seed rarely cross the sparse ridge of attack edges between the honest region and a sybil block, so landing probability inside the sybil region stays tiny however many fakes it holds. A fable of ten thousand internal edges cannot widen that cut; a walk's voyage from the seed ends in the honest region with overwhelming odds. Admitted sybil trust is bounded by the count of real honest-to-sybil edges — the cut width — not by headcount, since every walk escapes only through that narrow ridge.
